n2-he.meaning_mnemonic: A single <radical>step</radical> at the left edge, and beside it a hide being hauled off in one sheet — all <radical>skin</radical>, no animal left. Someone walked past carrying it a moment ago and is already down the road. You never saw the face, only the back of him. That man over there, the one you point at and cannot name: <radical>he</radical>.
n2-he.reading_mnemonic: Hii is the little intake of breath you make when the man in the skin cloak goes past without a word — 「<reading>ひ</reading>」 — and by the time you have finished it he is round the corner. Every single time you catch sight of him: ひ.

n2-zero.meaning_mnemonic: <radical>Rain</radical> across the whole top of the character, and underneath it a <radical>person</radical> kneeling on the bare <radical>ground</radical> while the clerk presses her <radical>stamp</radical> down onto the ledger. It lands in the column where this year's crop should have been counted, and what it prints there is one perfect round <radical>zero</radical>. The rain took the lot.
n2-zero.reading_mnemonic: Rei is that clerk. She is scrupulously polite about it — a small bow, a murmured 「<reading>れい</reading>」 — and then she inks the nothing into your row and moves down the line. れい, bow, zero. She has done it forty times today.

n2-nightfall.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>sun</radical> on the left has finally been let off: the shape on the right is the one that squeezes out from under the heavy lid and walks away <radical>exempt</radical>. Its shift is done, it has clocked out, and it drops below the roofline without waiting to be dismissed. The sun excused from duty is <radical>nightfall</radical>.
n2-nightfall.reading_mnemonic: Ban is the night watchman who takes over the moment the sun clocks off. He drags the gate shut and announces himself to the empty street — 「<reading>ばん</reading>」 — one flat syllable, every night, so you know the day is closed.

n2-second-1.meaning_mnemonic: A stalk of <radical>grain</radical> on the left, and beside it the <radical>small</radical> mark. Not the ear, not the stalk — one single bristle off the very top of the head, the thinnest thing on the entire plant. Slice up an hour the same way and the sliver you are left holding is one <radical>second</radical>.
n2-second-1.reading_mnemonic: Byou is the hospital timekeeper with the stopwatch, and she counts out loud in a flat clipped bark — 「<reading>びょう</reading>」, びょう, びょう — one for every tick. She will not speed up and she will not stop. びょう is a single second landing.

n2-end.meaning_mnemonic: Look at the <radical>tree</radical>: a <radical>stick</radical> straight up the middle, branches <radical>split</radical> away either side, and laid across the very top an extra <radical>lid</radical> of a stroke, drawn longer than the <radical>one</radical> below it. That top bar marks the last inch of the highest twig — as far up as this tree is ever going to go. The tip is the <radical>end</radical>.
n2-end.reading_mnemonic: Matsu is the woodsman who only ever takes the tip. He climbs the whole tree, snips the last bud off the top of it, and calls down 「<reading>まつ</reading>」 to say he has got there. まつ means there is nothing above him.

n2-ancestor.meaning_mnemonic: An <radical>altar</radical> stands on the left, and stacked on the right is an <radical>eye</radical> laid flat above a line of <radical>ground</radical> — a portrait propped up over the offerings, watching the room. Somebody long dead is looking back at you off that shelf. You bow to the face because it is your <radical>ancestor</radical>.
n2-ancestor.reading_mnemonic: So is the small catch of sound the incense makes when it takes light at the altar — 「<reading>そ</reading>」 — and for a second the eye in the portrait seems to move. One syllable, once a year, for the ancestor. そ.

n2-submit.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>person</radical> on the left, and on the right <radical>two</radical> bars stacked over a line of <radical>ground</radical>, carried on a <radical>stick</radical> each and <radical>split</radical> apart at the foot into a pair of legs. It is a tray on a stand, lifted with both hands. He is not setting it down — he is holding it up for somebody above him to take, which is what it is to <radical>submit</radical> a thing.
n2-submit.reading_mnemonic: Kyou is the offering-bearer who never lowers the tray. He walks the entire length of the hall with it over his head, announcing himself at every pillar — 「<reading>きょう</reading>」 — until somebody finally takes the weight off him.

n2-breath.meaning_mnemonic: Your own <radical>self</radical> sits on top — that nose you point at when you mean you — and directly underneath it, your <radical>heart</radical>. Nose above, heart below, and running between the two of them all day long is the one thing you never have to decide to do. In through the nose, down to the heart, back out: <radical>breath</radical>.
n2-breath.reading_mnemonic: Soku is the swimmer who comes up after far too long under and takes one enormous ragged gulp — 「<reading>そく</reading>」 — nose first, heart going like a hammer. That is what a breath you badly needed sounds like. そく.

n2-daughter.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>woman</radical> at the left, and beside her the whole shape of <radical>stopping</radical>: the eye that has seen something and the foot that will not take another step. She is planted in the doorway with her arms folded, and the young one is not going out tonight. A girl who gets stopped at the door is somebody's <radical>daughter</radical>.
n2-daughter.reading_mnemonic: Jou is how the neighbours refer to her, drawn out and a shade too formal — 「<reading>じょう</reading>」 — the sort of address you use for a girl of good family who is very definitely not allowed out. She hears じょう and rolls her eyes.

n2-heart.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>wide box</radical> of a room, and shoved right to the back of it a store of <radical>rice</radical> with something <radical>big</radical> planted on top of the pile. You have to walk through every other room in the house to reach it, and nobody outside the family ever does. The deepest room is the building's <radical>heart</radical>.
n2-heart.reading_mnemonic: Ou is the grandmother who lives in that back room and has not come out in years. Knock and you get one long syllable through the paper door — 「<reading>おう</reading>」 — meaning she heard you and no, you may not come in. おう, from the very back of the house.

n2-wife.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>woman</radical> at the bottom, and above her a <radical>broom</radical> held up on its <radical>stick</radical>, with a bar of <radical>ground</radical> ruled straight across the top. She is not sweeping out somebody else's household here. The broom, the floor and the roofline over both are hers, and the person who runs them is the <radical>wife</radical>.
n2-wife.reading_mnemonic: Sai is the one who actually decides. Ask her husband anything and he glances sideways at her first; she gives one flat 「<reading>さい</reading>」 and that is the answer on behalf of both of them. さい settles it.

n2-husband.meaning_mnemonic: Take the <radical>big</radical> figure — the <radical>person</radical> standing with both arms flung out wide — and lay one more bar across the top of it like a <radical>lid</radical>, so there are <radical>two</radical> horizontal strokes up there instead of one. That extra line is the pin through his topknot. He is grown, he is married, and he would like you to notice: <radical>husband</radical>.
n2-husband.reading_mnemonic: Fu is the same breath out through the nose you learned from his father, inherited exactly — arms folded in the doorway, one 「<reading>ふ</reading>」, no further comment offered. Getting married did not change it in the slightest.

n2-accomplished.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>sheep</radical> is being driven up a track: the <radical>road</radical> sweeps in underneath it, the surface <radical>splits</radical> into ruts, and packed <radical>earth</radical> climbs the whole way up. It is a long haul and the flock keeps stopping dead. But the last one is over the top and into the pen, and the job is <radical>accomplished</radical>.
n2-accomplished.reading_mnemonic: Tatsu is the drover who marks the top of every hill the same way: one slap on the gatepost and a barked 「<reading>たつ</reading>」 — done, next. He has said it at every gate between here and the coast. たつ means it is finished.

n2-on-foot.meaning_mnemonic: A single <radical>step</radical> at the left edge, and beside it the entire shape of a <radical>run</radical> — thigh forward, foot planting, ground coming loose behind. Except there is no horse here, no cart, and no road worth the name. Whatever is getting done today is getting done <radical>on foot</radical>.
n2-on-foot.reading_mnemonic: Toto the door-to-door turtle has never once taken a ride. He carries the sample doors on his shell and walks the entire round, and he announces himself at every house with the same syllable before he knocks — 「<reading>と</reading>」. と, and another mile.

n2-mister.meaning_mnemonic: Someone has swept the whole yard with a <radical>broom</radical>, one stroke that <radical>slides</radical> away to the left, until the <radical>ground</radical> is spotless. Then he opens his <radical>mouth</radical> and gives out tomorrow's orders. He is not the emperor, only the man directly above you — the <radical>mister</radical> whose name gets attached to every younger man in the room.
n2-mister.reading_mnemonic: Kun is the teacher who refuses to use first names. Every boy in the class gets the same syllable barked after his surname — 「<reading>くん</reading>」 — as the seating chart comes out. Tanaka-くん. Sato-くん. It is how you know he means you.

n2-yesterday.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>sun</radical> on the left, and on the right a <radical>stick</radical> driven upright into the dirt with one stroke that <radical>slides</radical> off it. That stick is a sundial, and the shadow it threw is still scratched into the ground beside it. The sun has moved on. The mark it left behind belongs to <radical>yesterday</radical>.
n2-yesterday.reading_mnemonic: Saku is the old gardener who checks his shadow-stick every dawn and then grumbles about how much better the light was 「<reading>さく</reading>」 — his one-word shorthand for the day before. Nothing is ever as good as さく was.
